name: camber_price_bands_2024
policy: CAMBER screening policy, not a standard, a tariff or a price forecast. Each band is an implied delivered price per MMBtu of billed energy (all charges divided by the energy, fixed charges included) that a correctly scaled U.S. commercial bill falls inside. The bands are deliberately wide: they exist to tell a bill read at the right scale from one read 1000x off, which moves the implied price by a factor of 1000, not to judge whether a price is fair. A price between the plausible band and the implausible bounds gives no verdict.
invariant: For every band, plausible_high / 1000 < implausible_below and plausible_low * 1000 > implausible_above, so a correctly scaled bill priced anywhere in its band places both 1000x readings beyond the implausible bounds.

sources.title: EIA Commercial Buildings Energy Consumption Survey 2018, Table C1 (consumption by major fuel) and Table C2 (expenditures by major fuel)
sources.observed: All buildings, 2018: electricity $118,997 million / 4,081 trillion Btu = $29.2 per MMBtu; natural gas $16,292 / 2,300 = $7.1; fuel oil $1,646 / 101 = $16.3; district heat (steam and hot water) $4,303 / 305 = $14.1.

bands.basis: $0.017 to $1.02 per kWh plausible; below $0.0012 or above $10.2 per kWh implausible. The 2024 state commercial averages span $0.072-0.382/kWh.
$1.5 to $150 per MMBtu plausible (a mostly fixed-charge summer bill can reach the top); the 2024 state commercial averages span about $6-36 per MMBtu.

CBECS 2018 district heat averaged $14.1 per MMBtu; district steam tariffs with demand and fixed charges run several times that. The band is CAMBER policy around that one national average; there is no public per-state steam price series.
As district steam (CBECS reports district heat as one fuel).

Per MMBtu of cooling delivered: $0.036 to $2.40 per ton-hour. No public national price series exists (CBECS does not report district chilled water expenditure); the band is CAMBER policy bracketing an electric chiller plant's cost of cooling (about $2-10 per MMBtu of cooling at $0.07-0.15/kWh and 0.6-1.2 kW/ton) with district demand and capacity charges on top. Unverified against a published tariff survey.
No. 1-6 fuel oil, diesel and kerosene. The EIA weekly series and the CBECS average sit at $16-30 per MMBtu.
The EIA weekly series sits at about $9-30 per MMBtu (wholesale to residential); small commercial deliveries carry tank and delivery charges.
